questions.question: A 68-year-old patient is brought to the clinic because of progressive memory problems, changes in personality, and difficulty controlling emotional responses. Which brain system is most closely associated with these functions?
A patient has a lesion involving the mammillary body. The neurologist explains that this structure is one of the grey matter components associated with the limbic system. Where is it located?
During an anatomical examination, a student observes a coiled mass of grey matter embedded at the edge of the temporal lobe. Its cross-section resembles a seahorse. Which structure is being examined?

A patient has damage to the fornix. During an anatomical discussion, the physician explains that the fornix passes below the corpus callosum and eventually divides into two rounded columns. Where do these columns normally terminate?

During a practical examination, a student identifies a large, comma-shaped mass of grey matter with a head, body, and tail. The head is related to the floor of the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle. Which structure is this?
A brain specimen shows a biconvex, lens-shaped basal ganglion. It consists of a darker lateral part and a paler medial part. Which of the following correctly identifies these two parts?
options: Globus pallidus laterally and putamen medially
Putamen laterally and globus pallidus medially
Caudate laterally and amygdaloid nucleus medially
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Putamen laterally and globus pallidus medially

questions.question: During a coronal section examination, a student identifies a thin sheet of grey matter lateral to the lentiform nucleus. It is separated from the lentiform nucleus by the external capsule and is related laterally to the extreme capsule. What is this structure?
A patient has damage to the white matter tract connecting the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies. Which structure is most likely affected?
During a brain imaging examination, a neurologist identifies the anterior limb of the internal capsule. Which two structures form its medial and lateral boundaries, respectively?
options: Head of caudate nucleus and anterior part of lentiform nucleus
Head of caudate nucleus and thalamus
Thalamus and posterior part of lentiform nucleus
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Head of caudate nucleus and anterior part of lentiform nucleus

questions.question: A lesion is detected in the posterior limb of the internal capsule. Which two structures are related to it medially and laterally, respectively?
options: Head of caudate nucleus and anterior part of lentiform nucleus
Thalamus and posterior part of lentiform nucleus
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Thalamus and posterior part of lentiform nucleus

questions.question: During an anatomical examination, a structure is found between the head of the caudate nucleus medially and the anterior part of the lentiform nucleus laterally. Which part of the internal capsule is being examined?
A patient has a lesion involving the internal capsule in the region between the thalamus and the posterior part of the lentiform nucleus. Which part is affected?
A patient has a lesion affecting nerve fibers responsible for connecting identical cortical areas in the right and left cerebral hemispheres. Which type of white matter fibers is affected?
During brain imaging, a large C-shaped bundle of white matter connecting the two cerebral hemispheres is found to be damaged. Which structure is involved?
A neurosurgeon identifies the largest commissure of the brain during an operation. Which structure is being identified?

During a sagittal section of the brain, a C-shaped mass of white fibers is observed on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere, lying in the floor of the median longitudinal cerebral fissure. Which structure is this?
A patient has a lesion affecting nerve fibers that connect adjacent gyri within the same cerebral hemisphere. Which type of fibers is damaged?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B. Short association fibers

questions.question: MRI reveals damage to a bundle of fibers connecting different lobes within the same cerebral hemisphere. Which of the following is the most likely affected structure?
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C. Superior longitudinal fasciculus

questions.question: A patient has a lesion affecting the largest commissure of the brain, which connects the two cerebral hemispheres. Which structure is involved?

During a radiological examination, a C-shaped white matter structure is identified on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere. Its enlarged posterior part contains fibers that curve backward toward the occipital lobes. Which part is being examined?

A patient has a lesion involving ascending and descending fibers connecting the cerebral cortex with subcortical centers and the spinal cord. These fibers radiate upward and outward from the internal capsule in a fan-like arrangement to reach the cortex. What is this arrangement called?
